text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Private VPC autoscaler reporting repeated provisioning failures and sustained GPU queue growth for customer 'EdgeTel' - severity: P1. Autoscale stuck in 'provisioning' state for 9m, backoff increasing.
alice-chen: Paging SRE rotation. I'm seeing 4000+ requests queued on the private cluster, tail latency > 20s, tail token generation failing with 503s. Confirming customer impact.
dmitri: I'm on it. What's the current nodepool size?
oncall-sre: Current nodepool (edgepool-nyc) shows desired=12, ready=4, provisioning=8, but kubelet never finishes join; logs show 'failed to allocate IP'  and imagepull backoff spikes.
carla: @dmitri any throttles from our CNI or VPC quotas? The VPC console shows ephemeral IP utilization at 98% for that subnet. Could be IP exhaustion.
dmitri: That matches. Also seeing repeated errors from our cluster-provisioner: "timeout waiting for bootstrap to register". Suspect customer subnet too small + allocator backpressure.
eng-infra: Jumping in — this customer uses our private package (on-premish) with subnet range /28, they should have requested /24. Will validate with account.
alice-chen: Immediate mitigation: can we route new warm jobs to hosted-fallback pool while we stabilize the private cluster? Need manual routing to avoid customer impact.
oncall-sre: We can set a routing policy for EdgeTel to fallback to hosted-dedicated for 10m. Doing now: `curl -X POST https://console.api/redwood/routing -d '{"customer":"EdgeTel","fallback":"hosted-dedicated","duration_min":10}'`
carla: :thumbsup: Please annotate the change so we can revert if not needed.
dmitri: While that's in flight, I'll try to force-allocate a node with a different IP allocation (use alternate-subnet). If that fails, we'll ask infra to expand the subnet or move customer to a new VPC.
incident-bot: page sent to oncall-sre via pagerduty-bot (PD-INC-9982)
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty: Alert acknowledged by oncall-sre. ETA to first action: 5m.
oncall-sre: Quick checks: `kubectl get nodes -o wide --selector=pool=edgepool-nyc`
```
NAME                           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP
edge-node-12                   NotReady   <none>   3m    v1.27.3   10.0.0.18      <none>
edge-node-13                   NotReady   <none>   2m    v1.27.3   10.0.0.19      <none>
```
Logs from bootstrap: `failed to configure network: ip allocator: no free addresses`
dmitri: Confirmed. Only 6 free IPs left but autoscaler trying to add 8. So it stalls and then backs off.
alice-chen: Customer impact: their live inference requests are degraded; some requests hitting fallback will be slower but succeeding. We should keep fallback in place until infra confirms subnet change.
eng-infra: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Reassign secondary CIDR to that VPC (fast if permissions ok), 2) Move EdgeTel routing to a different VPC with larger subnet, 3) Ask customer to expand their on-prem allocation (slower). Which do we prefer?
carla: Option 1 preferred. I'll request a secondary CIDR allocation now. Filing infra ticket and cc'ing security for the VPC change.
dmitri: Meanwhile I can temporarily reduce autoscaler desired to avoid thrashing (`kubectl patch hpa edgepool --patch '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'`) so we don't create half-provisioned nodes.
oncall-sre: Done. Reduced autoscaler pressure. Also applied sticky routing to favor hosted fallback so customer sessions won't split mid-request.
alice-chen: Good. Keep logs of token/310 errors for postmortem. Flagging this for incident postmortem and customer comms.
incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation steps applied: fallback routing enabled, autoscaler min set, infra request for secondary CIDR opened. Escalation: eng-infra oncall.
pagerduty-bot: PD: Reminder scheduled for 30m to reevaluate.
dmitri: Infra confirmed secondary CIDR allocated, applying to VPC now. Might take ~3m for route propagation.
eng-infra: Applied. New IPs available. I'm triggering node provisioning reset for stuck instances.
```
# command
for node in edge-node-12 edge-node-13; do ssh root@$node 'systemctl restart kubelet && journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 20'; done
```
eng-infra: Nodes joined successfully, ready=12. Queue drained from 4k -> 200 in 7m. Latency returning to normal.
alice-chen: :tada: Customer routed back to private cluster. Reverting fallback routing in 5m.
carla: Filing postmortem: probable root cause = insufficient CIDR for private VPC, autoscaler didn't gracefully fallback. Actions: require CIDR sizing check on onboarding doc + autoscaler change to detect IP exhaustion and mark pool unhealthy.
dmitri: I'll open issue in eng-runtime to add explicit IP exhaustion metric and failover hook.
oncall-sre: Closing pager, but leaving incident open for postmortem write-up. Final status: mitigated, customer impact reduced via hosted fallback, infra expanded subnet, cluster stable.
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> mitigated at 1755009445. Please add notes to /incidents/postmortems/ when ready.
